1	# Agent skills module: design and plan
2	
3	## Starter prompt (paste this to begin the next session)
4	
5	> I want one version-tracked copy of each of my personal agent skills, linked
6	> into every harness I use (pi via `~/.agents/skills`, Claude Code via
7	> `~/.claude/skills`, Kiro via `~/.kiro/skills`). Read
8	> `docs/plans/2026-10-11-agent-skills-module-design.md` first, then implement
9	> Phase 1 only: the `webframp.agentSkills` module plus migrating
10	> `writing-editorial`. Stop after Phase 1 verification and show me the results
11	> before touching any other skill.
12	
13	## Goal
14	
15	Personal skills live once, in this repo, under git. Home-manager links each one
16	into every harness's skill directory, so the content every harness reads is
17	byte-identical by construction and every change (including edits made by
18	agents) shows up in `git diff`.
19	
20	Skills installed and upgraded by other tools (swamp) stay out of scope and
21	must never be touched by this module.
22	
23	## Why
24	
25	- **Drift already happened.** Four skills exist as separate copies in both
26	  `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.kiro/skills`, and all four differ (details in
27	  "Current state"). Nothing records which copy is newer or why.
28	- **Agents edit skills.** Skills are instructions that future agent sessions
29	  obey. An edit by any session or tool silently changes behavior. Git makes
30	  every change reviewable and revertible; this is also a supply-chain concern
31	  (see the `agentic-security` skill).
32	- **Multiple hosts.** This flake configures bluestreak, galvatron-wsl,
33	  ubuntu-wsl, and generic. Skills should follow the user like the rest of the
34	  config.
35	- **Regressions.** When a skill rewrite makes output worse, `git log -p` on
36	  its `SKILL.md` shows exactly what changed.
37	
38	## Current state (as of 2026-10-11, on galvatron-wsl)
39	
40	### Skill directories
41	
42	| Path | Read by | Managed by today |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| `~/.agents/skills/` | pi (native default), other Agent Skills harnesses | swamp (`swamp`, `swamp-getting-started`) + one manual skill |
45	| `~/.claude/skills/` | Claude Code | manual copies; swamp copies; Claude-managed `synced/` and `.trash/` |
46	| `~/.kiro/skills/` | Kiro CLI | manual copies; swamp copies |
47	
48	None of these directories is a git repo or managed by home-manager.
49	
50	### writing-editorial (the Phase 1 skill)
51	
52	Rewritten in the previous session (from Klinkenborg's *Several Short Sentences
53	About Writing*). Current layout, set up by hand:
54	
55	```
56	~/.agents/skills/writing-editorial/SKILL.md      real directory (canonical today)
57	~/.claude/skills/writing-editorial -> ~/.agents/skills/writing-editorial
58	~/.kiro/skills/writing-editorial   -> ~/.agents/skills/writing-editorial
59	```
60	
61	Verified working through those single-hop symlinks in all three harnesses
62	(see "Verification" for the commands). The pre-rewrite version was backed up
63	to a session scratchpad that will not survive; git history starts with the
64	rewritten version.
65	
66	### Drifted skills (exist in both Claude and Kiro, contents differ)
67	
68	| Skill | Claude copy | Kiro copy | Nature of the difference |
69	|---|---|---|---|
70	| `hostile-code-analysis` | 2026-08-01, 8523 B | 2026-07-30, 8505 B | Frontmatter only: Claude copy has single-line description plus `metadata.version: 2026-07-30`; Kiro copy has folded description |
71	| `triage` | 2026-08-02 | 2026-07-30 | Harness wording: Claude says "project's CLAUDE.md (Release Notes section)" and "activate the hostile-code-analysis skill"; Kiro says "extension-conventions steering" and offers a project-level `skills/hostile-code-analysis.md` fallback |
72	| `pre-push-review` | 2026-08-10, 10752 B | 2026-08-13, 12455 B | Kiro copy is newer and adds a whole section, "2c. Swamp Extension Version and Manifest Gates" (manifest/model version alignment, upgrade chain, `swamp extension fmt/quality/push --dry-run`) that the Claude copy lacks |
73	| `loadgen-fleet` | 2026-08-02, 28673 B | 2026-07-31, 12426 B | Substantially rewritten; Claude copy is more than twice the size, with a different description |
74	
75	Run `diff -r ~/.claude/skills/<name> ~/.kiro/skills/<name>` to see each in full.
76	
77	### Single-harness skills (candidates for later promotion)
78	
79	- Claude only: `agentic-security`, `bench`, `extension-compliance-audit`,
80	  `infrastructure-philosophy`, `systematic-debugging`, `using-git-worktrees`,
81	  `writing-plans`.
82	- Kiro only: `adversarial-review`, `bench-harness`, `design-review`,
83	  `exe.dev`, `extension-development`, `jetpack`, `pr-fix-loop`,
84	  `release-review`, `search-tech-docs`, `swamp-code-review`.
85	- Already identical in both: `doc-writing` (plus the swamp-managed pair).
86	
87	Notes: `bench` (Claude) and `bench-harness` (Kiro) may be the same skill under
88	two names. The Kiro directory `exe.dev` declares `name: using-exe-dev`, which
89	violates the Agent Skills rule that `name` matches the directory name and
90	contains only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.
91	
92	## Design
93	
94	### Source location: `config/skills/<name>/`
95	
96	Matches the existing `config/claude/`, `config/pi/`, `config/doom/` layout.
97	Each skill is a directory with `SKILL.md` and optional `references/`,
98	`scripts/`, `assets/`.
99	
100	### Module: `modules/home-manager/agent-skills.nix`
101	
102	Follow the repo conventions in `AGENTS.md`: two `# ABOUTME:` header lines,
103	`webframp.*` namespace, export from `modules/home-manager/default.nix`.
104	
105	Proposed options:
106	
107	```nix
108	options.webframp.agentSkills = {
109	  enable = lib.mkEnableOption "personal agent skills linked into every harness";
110	
111	  skills = lib.mkOption {
112	    type = lib.types.listOf lib.types.str;
113	    default = [];
114	    description = "Skill directory names under config/skills to link.";
115	  };
116	
117	  targets = lib.mkOption {
118	    type = lib.types.listOf (lib.types.enum ["agents" "claude" "kiro"]);
119	    default = ["agents" "claude" "kiro"];
120	    description = "Harness skill directories to link into.";
121	  };
122	};
123	```
124	
125	Target paths: `agents` = `~/.agents/skills`, `claude` = `~/.claude/skills`,
126	`kiro` = `~/.kiro/skills`.
127	
128	Enable in `home/sme/shared/base.nix` next to `webframp.claudeCode.enable`,
129	with `skills = ["writing-editorial"];`. List options merge, so a host can add
130	skills without repeating the shared list.
131	
132	### Decision: explicit list, not auto-discovery
133	
134	`builtins.readDir ./config/skills` would make adding a skill zero-config, but
135	it hides what each host gets and makes per-host subsets awkward. The explicit
136	list costs one line per skill and reads clearly. Either way, flake evaluation
137	only sees git-tracked files, so a new skill must be `git add`ed before
138	`make switch` (this is a common surprise; document it in the module comment).
139	
140	Add an assertion that every listed name has `config/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in
141	the flake source, so a typo fails at build time instead of producing a
142	dangling link.
143	
144	### Decision: direct activation symlinks, not `home.file` + `mkOutOfStoreSymlink`
145	
146	`modules/home-manager/claude-code.nix` documents why: `home.file` with
147	`mkOutOfStoreSymlink` produces a double-hop symlink (target -> home-files store
148	profile -> dotfiles). Claude Code's atomic writer (write `.tmp`, then rename)
149	resolves only one hop, lands in the read-only store, and fails with `EROFS`.
150	Agents edit skills with exactly that kind of writer, so skills need the same
151	treatment: one `ln -s` from the harness directory straight to the working copy.
152	
153	It is not verified whether the double hop breaks directory symlinks the way it
154	breaks `settings.json`. Use the direct pattern anyway, for consistency and
155	because the failure mode only appears when an agent tries to edit a skill.
156	
157	Single-hop symlinks to a directory are verified to work in all three harnesses
158	(that is the current `writing-editorial` setup). Pi deduplicates skills by
159	canonical path, so the same skill reached through several links will not
160	produce name-collision warnings.
161	
162	### Activation script requirements
163	
164	Run with `lib.hm.dag.entryAfter ["writeBoundary"]`, like `linkClaudeSettings`.
165	For each target directory and each skill:
166	
167	1. `mkdir -p` the target directory.
168	2. If `<target>/<name>` is a symlink, replace it with `ln -sfn`.
169	3. If `<target>/<name>` is a **real directory or file**, do not touch it. Print
170	   a warning naming the path and skip that link. Do not fail the whole switch
171	   for one skill, and never delete user content.
172	   - **Gotcha:** `ln -sfn src dest` when `dest` is an existing real directory
173	     creates `dest/<name>` *inside* it instead of replacing it. Check with
174	     `[ -L ]` / `[ -e ]` before linking.
175	4. If nothing is there, create the link.
176	
177	Cleanup of removed skills: write the list of links created to a state file
178	(e.g. `~/.local/state/webframp-agent-skills/links`). On the next activation,
179	remove any previously recorded link that is no longer wanted, **only if** it
180	is still a symlink whose target is inside `config/skills/`. This guarantees
181	the module never removes anything it did not create.
182	
183	Use `run` for mutating commands so `home-manager switch --dry-run` stays
184	honest (as `claude-code.nix` does).
185	
186	### Never touch
187	
188	- `swamp`, `swamp-getting-started`, or any other swamp-installed skill. Swamp
189	  writes identical copies into all three directories and upgrades them itself.
190	- `~/.claude/skills/synced/` and `~/.claude/skills/.trash/` (managed by Claude).
191	- Any entry not in `webframp.agentSkills.skills`.
192	
193	### Content rules (one copy must serve every harness)
194	
195	- Frontmatter uses only Agent Skills spec fields: `name` (must equal the
196	  directory name; lowercase letters, digits, single hyphens; at most 64
197	  characters), `description` (at most 1024 characters), and optionally
198	  `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata`, `allowed-tools`. Avoid
199	  harness-specific fields.
200	- Write instructions in harness-neutral terms ("the project's agent
201	  instructions file" rather than "CLAUDE.md" or "steering").
202	- When a skill truly needs harness-specific steps, put them in
203	  `references/<harness>.md` and tell the reader in `SKILL.md` when to load
204	  each one. Never fork the skill directory per harness; forking is what caused
205	  the current drift.
206	
207	## Phases
208	
209	### Phase 1: module plus writing-editorial
210	
211	1. Do not include unrelated work in the commit. At planning time the working
212	   tree already had uncommitted changes in `config/claude/settings.json`,
213	   `flake.lock`, `flake.nix`, `home/sme/shared/base.nix`,
214	   `home/sme/shared/includes/herdr.toml`, `pkgs/swamp/default.nix`, plus
215	   untracked `.swamp/`, `BOOTSTRAP.md`, and two other plans. Check
216	   `git status` and ask before touching any of them. `base.nix` has
217	   pre-existing edits, so stage only your hunk.
218	2. Create `config/skills/` and move the real directory into it:
219	   `mv ~/.agents/skills/writing-editorial config/skills/writing-editorial`.
220	3. Remove the two manual symlinks (`~/.claude/skills/writing-editorial`,
221	   `~/.kiro/skills/writing-editorial`). Confirm they are symlinks with
222	   `ls -la` first.
223	4. Write the module, export it in `modules/home-manager/default.nix`, enable
224	   it in `base.nix`.
225	5. `git add` the new files (flake eval ignores untracked files), then run
226	   `make fmt` and `make check`.
227	6. Build, diff, and apply. galvatron-wsl is the only entry in
228	   `VALID_NIXOS_HOSTS` (home-manager runs as a NixOS module there), so use
229	   `make nixos-build`, `make nixos-diff`, `make nixos-switch`. Other hosts use
230	   `make build`, `make diff`, `make switch`.
231	7. Run every check in "Verification". Report results and stop.
232	
233	### Phase 2: reconcile the four drifted skills
234	
235	One skill at a time, with the user deciding. For each: show the full diff,
236	propose a merged harness-neutral version (for example, `pre-push-review`
237	should keep Kiro's section 2c; `triage` needs neutral wording for the
238	instructions-file and steering references), get approval, then move it into
239	`config/skills/`, move both old copies out of the way, add it to the list, and
240	switch. `loadgen-fleet` is the largest rewrite; expect a real decision there,
241	not a mechanical merge.
242	
243	### Phase 3: promote single-harness skills
244	
245	Ask which of the single-harness skills should become shared. Resolve the
246	`bench` / `bench-harness` question and fix the `exe.dev` name/directory
247	mismatch while promoting.
248	
249	### Phase 4 (optional): validation target
250	
251	A `make skills-check` that checks every `config/skills/*/SKILL.md` for: `name`
252	equal to the directory, the name character rules, description length of at
253	most 1024, and only spec frontmatter fields. Pi's loader can serve as the
254	validator (see below); a small script would avoid depending on pi's internals.
255	
256	## Verification
257	
258	Run after every switch that changes skills.
259	
260	```bash
261	# 1. Every harness path resolves to the same file in the working copy
262	for d in ~/.agents ~/.claude ~/.kiro; do
263	  readlink -f "$d/skills/writing-editorial/SKILL.md"
264	done   # all three should print .../dotfiles/config/skills/writing-editorial/SKILL.md
265	
266	# 2. Exactly one symlink hop (not a store path in between)
267	for d in ~/.agents ~/.claude ~/.kiro; do readlink "$d/skills/writing-editorial"; done
268	
269	# 3. Kiro lists it
270	WAYLAND_DISPLAY= kiro-cli chat --no-interactive \
271	  "Without using tools, list only the names of the skills available to you, one per line."
272	
273	# 4. Pi parses it without diagnostics. `pi -p` fails on this host with
274	#    "Could not load credentials from any providers", so call pi's loader
275	#    directly. Store paths change with each pi upgrade; find them via
276	#    `readlink -f ~/.nix-profile/bin/pi` and the wrapper scripts it execs.
277	NODE=<pi's node, e.g. /nix/store/...-nodejs-24.x/bin/node>
278	PI=<pi package>/lib/node_modules/pi-monorepo
279	"$NODE" --input-type=module -e "
280	const m = await import('$PI/dist/core/skills.js');
281	const r = m.loadSkills({ cwd: '/tmp', includeDefaults: false,
282	  skillPaths: [process.env.HOME + '/.agents/skills'] });
283	console.log(r.skills.map(s => s.name), JSON.stringify(r.diagnostics));"
284	```
285	
286	5. Claude Code: start a fresh session and confirm `writing-editorial` appears in
287	   the available-skills list with the new description (it begins "Editorial
288	   principles for prose, drawing on Benjamin Dreyer").
289	6. Edit test: in a Claude Code session, have it make a trivial edit to the
290	   skill through `~/.claude/skills/writing-editorial/SKILL.md`; confirm the
291	   change appears in `git diff` in this repo with no `EROFS` error, then
292	   revert it.
293	7. Confirm swamp's skills are untouched: `ls -la ~/.{agents,claude,kiro}/skills/swamp`
294	   should still be real directories.
295	
296	Note: `loadSkills({ includeDefaults: true })` only scans `~/.pi/agent/skills`
297	and `.pi/skills`; pi adds `~/.agents/skills` through its package manager
298	(`dist/core/package-manager.js`). An empty result from `includeDefaults: true`
299	does not mean discovery is broken.
300	
301	## References
302	
303	### This repo
304	
305	- `AGENTS.md`: host table, `webframp.*` namespace, ABOUTME headers, `make`
306	  targets, the "fail loud" convention (Doom `+local.el`).
307	- `modules/home-manager/claude-code.nix`: the double-hop `EROFS` rationale and
308	  the direct activation-symlink pattern to copy.
309	- `modules/home-manager/pi.nix`, `modules/home-manager/doom.nix`: the
310	  `mkOutOfStoreSymlink` pattern (fine for files pi and Doom only read).
311	- `modules/home-manager/default.nix`: module export list.
312	- `home/sme/shared/base.nix`: where shared `webframp.*` modules are enabled.
313	- `docs/plans/2026-10-09-herdr-keybindings-followup.md`: format of a previous
314	  hand-off plan.
315	
316	### External
317	
318	- Agent Skills specification: https://agentskills.io/specification
319	- Pi skills documentation, shipped with the package (v0.87.1 at planning time):
320	  `<pi package>/lib/node_modules/pi-monorepo/docs/skills.md`. Key points: pi
321	  implements the spec; it discovers `~/.agents/skills` and project
322	  `.agents/skills`; it recurses into directories until it finds `SKILL.md`; it
323	  does not enforce name equal to directory, but other harnesses may.
324	- Pi `CHANGELOG.md` in the same package: symlinked skill directories are
325	  followed and deduplicated by canonical path (entries for #304, #3417, #3818).
326	- Claude Code skills documentation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills
327	- Kiro CLI: reads `~/.kiro/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and follows directory
328	  symlinks (verified on 2026-10-10 with the `kiro-cli chat --no-interactive`
329	  check above).
330	
331	### Related user skills
332	
333	- `writing-editorial`: the first skill to migrate.
334	- `agentic-security`: background on skills as a supply-chain surface.
335

> ### 2c. Swamp Extension Version and Manifest Gates
> 
> When changes touch swamp extensions (any directory with a `manifest.yaml`),
> run these additional checks BEFORE the adversarial review. These fail
> frequently and are easy to miss:
> 
> 1. **Version alignment.** The `version` field in `manifest.yaml` MUST match
>    the `version` field in the model's TypeScript source (`export const model =
>    { version: "..." }`). If you bumped the model version, bump the manifest.
>    Verify with `swamp extension version --manifest manifest.yaml --json`.
> 
> 2. **Upgrade chain integrity.** If the model has an `upgrades` array, the last
>    entry's `toVersion` MUST equal the model's `version` field. Every upgrade
>    entry MUST have a unique `toVersion` in ascending order. A version bump
>    without a corresponding upgrade entry means cached data from the previous
>    version will not be migrated.
> 
> 3. **Manifest format validation.** Run `swamp extension fmt manifest.yaml
>    --check --json`. This catches YAML formatting issues that the push rejects.
> 
> 4. **Quality gate.** Run `swamp extension quality manifest.yaml --json`.
>    Verify `status: "passed"` and no degraded checks.
> 
> 5. **Dry-run push.** Run `swamp extension push manifest.yaml --dry-run`.
>    This exercises the full bundler, archive builder, and schema validation
>    pipeline. If it fails here, it fails in CI.
> 
> **Common failure modes:**
> - Bumping `model.version` but not `manifest.yaml` version
> - Adding an upgrade handler but using the wrong `toVersion` string
> - Forgetting to add `days` or `fetchedAt` to a new resource spec that
>   requires it (schema validation fails on push)
> - Leaving the old spec name in a `writeResource` call after renaming specs
